ReadBuffer.overview: Simplified interface for reading relation blocks using default parameters and main fork access.

ReadBufferExtended.overview: Comprehensive buffer reading function supporting multiple read modes, fork selection, and buffer access strategies for relation block access.

ReadBuffer_common.overview: Central unified function implementing common logic for all ReadBuffer variants, handling different read modes and delegating to appropriate buffer management functions.

ReadBufferWithoutRelcache.overview: Reads a buffer without requiring a relation cache entry, used during WAL replay and recovery.

ReadRecentBuffer.overview: Optimized buffer access function that attempts to pin a block using a recently observed buffer identifier, avoiding buffer table lookups.

StartReadBuffers.overview: Public API for initiating asynchronous read operations on multiple contiguous database blocks with scatter-gather I/O optimization.

WaitReadBuffers.overview: Performs asynchronous batch reading of multiple database pages from storage, implementing scatter-gather I/O and handling both local and shared buffer validation.

PinBufferForBlock.overview: Core internal function that pins a buffer for a given block, handling both shared and local buffers with appropriate I/O context and statistics tracking.

BufferAlloc.overview: Core buffer allocation logic for shared buffers: lookup, victim selection, and buffer pool management without performing actual I/O operations.

GetVictimBuffer.overview: Finds and prepares a buffer to be reused by evicting its current contents, handling dirty buffers and ensuring proper cleanup.

PinBuffer.overview: Makes a shared buffer unavailable for replacement by incrementing its reference count and managing usage count based on the access strategy.

PinBuffer_Locked.overview: Pins a buffer that is already locked via buffer header spinlock, used when the caller already holds the BM_LOCKED flag.

UnpinBuffer.overview: Decrements the pin count of a shared buffer and removes it from the current resource owner's buffer tracking, making buffer available for replacement.

ReleaseBuffer.overview: Primary public interface for unpinning both shared and local buffers in PostgreSQL's buffer management system.

UnlockReleaseBuffer.overview: Convenience function that unlocks a buffer's content lock and releases the buffer pin in a single operation.

ReleaseAndReadBuffer.overview: Combines releasing a currently pinned buffer and reading a new buffer, optimizing when the same buffer is already loaded.

LockBuffer.overview: Acquires or releases the content lock for a buffer, providing exclusive or shared access to buffer contents.

ConditionalLockBuffer.overview: Non-blocking function that attempts to acquire exclusive content lock on a buffer without waiting.

LockBufferForCleanup.overview: Acquires exclusive lock on a buffer and waits until no other backends hold pins, enabling safe deletion of items from the buffer.

LockBufHdr.overview: Acquires exclusive lock on a buffer header by atomically setting the BM_LOCKED flag in the buffer state.

StartBufferIO.overview: Initiates I/O operations on a buffer by setting the BM_IO_IN_PROGRESS flag, ensuring only one process performs I/O on a buffer at a time.

TerminateBufferIO.overview: Completes I/O operations on a buffer by clearing BM_IO_IN_PROGRESS, updating buffer state flags, and notifying waiting processes.

WaitIO.overview: Blocks the current process until the IO_IN_PROGRESS flag on a specified buffer is cleared, ensuring I/O operations complete before proceeding.

MarkBufferDirty.overview: Marks a buffer's contents as modified (dirty), indicating data needs writing to disk during next checkpoint or buffer eviction.

MarkBufferDirtyHint.overview: Marks a buffer dirty for non-critical hint bit updates, with special handling for WAL logging and race conditions.

FlushBuffer.overview: Physically writes a shared buffer's contents to disk, implementing WAL-before-data rule and handling checksums, I/O tracking, and buffer state management.

BufferSync.overview: Writes out all dirty buffers in the shared buffer pool to disk, implementing core checkpoint buffer synchronization with load balancing across tablespaces.

SyncOneBuffer.overview: Processes a single buffer during checkpoint or background writer operations, determining if the buffer needs writing and performing the actual I/O.

CheckPointBuffers.overview: Flushes all dirty blocks in the buffer pool to disk during checkpoint operations, ensuring data durability at specific recovery points.

BgBufferSync.overview: Periodically writes out dirty buffers in the background, implementing LRU-based buffer cleaning with sophisticated allocation rate tracking and adaptive scanning.

InitBufferPool.overview: Initializes the shared buffer pool during shared-memory initialization: buffer descriptors, buffer blocks, condition variables, and checkpoint data structures.

BufferShmemSize.overview: Calculates total shared memory required for PostgreSQL's buffer pool: buffer descriptors, data pages, condition variables, and related structures.

InitBufferPoolAccess.overview: Initializes a backend's access to the shared buffer pool by setting up private reference counting and registering cleanup handlers.

StrategyGetBuffer.overview: Core buffer replacement function: selects next candidate buffer using either ring buffer strategy or clock sweep algorithm.

StrategyFreeBuffer.overview: Adds a buffer to the free list, making it available for immediate reuse.

StrategyRejectBuffer.overview: Allows buffer manager to reconsider buffer selection when a chosen dirty buffer would require expensive WAL flushing, optimized for bulk read.

StrategyInitialize.overview: Initializes the buffer cache replacement strategy including buffer lookup hashtable and shared strategy control structures.

StrategySyncStart.overview: Provides background buffer sync process with optimal starting point for synchronization and buffer allocation activity statistics.

StrategyNotifyBgWriter.overview: Sets or clears allocation notification latch for background writer process to enable wake-up from hibernation.

GetAccessStrategy.overview: Creates a BufferAccessStrategy object with predefined ring sizes for different access patterns (BULKREAD=256KB, BULKWRITE=16MB, VACUUM=2MB).

BufferStrategyControl.overview: Shared control structure for the buffer replacement strategy: spinlock, clock sweep hand, freelist head/tail, and allocation statistics.

BufferAccessStrategyData.overview: Private per-backend structure for ring buffer strategy: tracks buffer ring slots for strategies like BAS_BULKREAD, BAS_BULKWRITE, BAS_VACUUM.

BufTableLookup.overview: Looks up a BufferTag in the shared buffer mapping hash table, returning buffer ID or -1 if not found.

BufTableInsert.overview: Inserts a hashtable entry for a given tag and buffer ID, returning -1 on success or existing buffer ID on conflict.

BufTableDelete.overview: Deletes a hashtable entry for a given tag (which must exist). Caller must hold exclusive lock on BufMappingLock.

BufTableHashCode.overview: Computes hash code for a BufferTag to determine buffer partition locking.

InitBufTable.overview: Initializes the shared memory hash table for buffer tag to buffer ID mapping.

BufferDesc.overview: Shared descriptor/state data for a single shared buffer: tag, state (atomic), wait_backend_pgprocno, freeNext, content_lock. Kept under 64 bytes for cache line alignment.

BufferTag.overview: Identifies which disk block a buffer contains: spcOid, dbOid, relNumber, forkNum, blockNum. Used as hash key in buffer mapping table.

BufferLookupEnt.overview: Entry for buffer lookup hashtable: maps BufferTag key to buffer ID.

InvalidateBuffer.overview: Marks a shared buffer as invalid and returns it to the freelist, handling complex synchronization for safe buffer reclamation during relation drops.

DropRelationBuffers.overview: Removes pages of specified relation forks from the buffer pool with block numbers >= firstDelBlock, used during file deletion or truncation.

DropRelationsAllBuffers.overview: Removes all pages of all forks from multiple relations from the buffer pool.

FlushRelationBuffers.overview: Writes all dirty pages of a specific relation to disk, ensuring kernel has up-to-date view of relation data.

FlushOneBuffer.overview: Flushes a previously locked and pinned buffer to the OS, providing a simple interface for flushing a single specific buffer.

FlushDatabaseBuffers.overview: Writes all dirty buffers for a given database to disk.

PageHeaderData.overview: Fundamental structure defining header layout for all PostgreSQL database pages: pd_lsn, pd_checksum, pd_flags, pd_lower, pd_upper, pd_special, pd_pagesize_version, pd_prune_xid, pd_linp[].

PageInit.overview: Initializes page contents in the buffer pool, setting up basic page structure and metadata without calculating initial checksum.

PageAddItemExtended.overview: Adds an item to a page at a specified or automatically determined offset, handling space allocation, line pointer management, and data placement.

PageRepairFragmentation.overview: Removes fragmentation from a heap page by eliminating unused line pointers and compacting remaining tuples.

PageGetFreeSpace.overview: Returns size of free (allocatable) space on a page, reduced by space needed for a new line pointer.

PageGetHeapFreeSpace.overview: Returns free space on a heap page with heap-specific line pointer limits enforced.

PageIsVerifiedExtended.overview: Validates page header and checksum when page is read from disk, providing protection against corrupted data.

PageSetChecksumCopy.overview: Creates a copy of a page with calculated checksum for safe writing, protecting against concurrent modifications.

PageSetChecksumInplace.overview: Calculates and sets checksum directly on a page in private memory, used when concurrent modifications are guaranteed not to occur.

XLogFlush.overview: Ensures all WAL data through a specified position is flushed to disk, implementing group commit optimization and handling both normal and recovery scenarios.

PageGetLSN.overview: Returns the LSN (Log Sequence Number) stored in a page header, used to enforce WAL-before-data rule.

PageSetLSN.overview: Sets the LSN value in a page header after WAL record insertion.

BufferGetLSNAtomic.overview: Returns page LSN with atomic semantics suitable for concurrent access without holding content lock.

smgropen.overview: Returns an SMgrRelation object for the specified relation, creating if necessary, with transaction-scoped lifetime management.

smgrread.overview: Lightweight inline wrapper function that reads a single block from storage into a buffer.

smgrwrite.overview: Lightweight inline wrapper that writes a single block from a buffer to storage.

smgrreadv.overview: Reads a range of blocks from a relation into multiple supplied buffers in a single vectorized operation.

smgrwritev.overview: Performs vectorized write operations on existing blocks of a relation.

smgrextend.overview: Adds a new block to a relation file, extending the file beyond its current end-of-file position.

smgrprefetch.overview: Initiates asynchronous read operations for specified blocks to improve I/O performance through prefetching.

smgrnblocks.overview: Returns number of blocks in a relation, utilizing caching to optimize repeated queries.

smgrwriteback.overview: Triggers kernel writeback for a specified range of blocks, encouraging OS to write dirty pages to disk.

smgrimmedsync.overview: Forces relation to stable storage synchronously, primarily used for building new relations where WAL logging is bypassed.

mdreadv.overview: Performs vectored read operations on multiple blocks from a relation, handling segment boundaries, short reads, and error conditions.

mdwritev.overview: Writes multiple database blocks at appropriate locations within relation files for updating already-existing blocks.

mdextend.overview: Extends a relation by adding a block at specified position, writing beyond the current end-of-file.

mdwriteback.overview: Tells kernel to write pages back to storage, flushing multiple consecutive blocks from buffer cache to disk.

mdnblocks.overview: Retrieves total number of blocks in a relation, with side effect of opening all active segments.

WritebackContext.overview: Structure managing batching and coordination of pending writeback requests in buffer management system.

WritebackContextInit.overview: Initializes a WritebackContext for managing batching of dirty buffer writebacks with configurable coalescing limits.

IssuePendingWritebacks.overview: Issues all pending writeback requests previously scheduled to the OS for improved IO scheduling performance.

ScheduleBufferTagForWriteback.overview: Adds a dirty buffer to the pending writeback queue for batched I/O operations.

PrefetchBuffer.overview: High-level interface for prefetching relation blocks that routes to appropriate buffer pool implementation based on relation type.

PrefetchSharedBuffer.overview: Implements buffer prefetching for shared buffers by checking cache and initiating asynchronous I/O if needed.

LocalBufferAlloc.overview: Finds or creates a local buffer for a page of a temporary relation. Local buffer equivalent of BufferAlloc.

PinLocalBuffer.overview: Pins a local buffer by incrementing its reference count, preventing reuse while the buffer is being accessed.

UnpinLocalBuffer.overview: Unpins a local buffer, making it available for replacement by subsequent local buffer allocation.

MarkLocalBufferDirty.overview: Marks a local buffer as dirty, indicating data needs writing back when buffer is recycled.

InitLocalBuffers.overview: Initializes local buffer structures on first use in a session, allocating descriptors and setting up the local hash table.

GetLocalBufferStorage.overview: Allocates memory for local buffers using an efficient block allocation strategy to minimize memory management overhead.

ExtendBufferedRel.overview: Convenience wrapper that extends a buffered relation by exactly one block.

EvictUnpinnedBuffer.overview: Attempts to evict the current block in a shared buffer, intended for testing and development only.
